guarantees.claim: If hash_start is asserted, message_length_d is driven to all zeros.
If hash_start is deasserted and msg_write, sha_en, and packer_ready are all asserted, message_length_d is set to message_length + 64'(wmask_ones).

When hash_start is low, the write condition (msg_write & sha_en & packer_ready) is false, cfg_block is low, and reg2hw.msg_length_lower.qe is true, the lower 32 bits of message_length_d are driven from reg2hw.msg_length_lower.q.

When hash_start is low, the write condition (msg_write & sha_en & packer_ready) is false, cfg_block is low, and reg2hw.msg_length_upper.qe is true, the upper 32 bits of message_length_d are driven from reg2hw.msg_length_upper.q.
When none of the overriding conditions (hash_start, msg_write & sha_en & packer_ready, or !cfg_block with a qe set) are true, message_length_d holds the current message_length value.

assumptions.claim: reg2hw.msg_length_lower.q and reg2hw.msg_length_upper.q hold valid length values when their qe bits are set and cfg_block is low.
assumptions.risk: Message length may be loaded with garbage, corrupting HMAC length tracking.

assumptions.claim: wmask_ones accurately reflects the number of valid bytes in the current data write when msg_write, sha_en, and packer_ready are active.
assumptions.risk: message_length_d will be incremented incorrectly, leading to HMAC length mismatch and potential integrity failure.

assumptions.claim: hash_start is asserted only at the start of a new message and does not coincide with a msg_write that must be counted for that message; this RTL discards any concurrent write.
assumptions.risk: Loss of write contribution causes HMAC to be computed over a shorter effective message, breaking authenticity.

assumptions.claim: cfg_block is asserted by the system to ignore software writes to the message length registers when those writes should not affect the current hash.
assumptions.risk: If cfg_block is incorrectly low during a hash, register writes could alter message_length_d, compromising HMAC integrity.

uncertain_points.claim: If cfg_block is deasserted and a register write occurs while the hash engine is active (after hash_start), message_length_d can be changed, potentially corrupting the final HMAC. Is cfg_block guaranteed to be high during hash operations?
uncertain_points.cond: cfg_block == 0 and hash_start has been asserted but hash not yet done
uncertain_points.risk: An attacker or faulty software could alter the message length mid-hash, breaking integrity or enabling chosen-prefix attacks.

uncertain_points.claim: When hash_start and msg_write assert in the same cycle, the write contribution is lost because hash_start clears message_length_d with higher priority. Is this the intended protocol?
uncertain_points.cond: hash_start == 1 and msg_write == 1 and sha_en == 1 and packer_ready == 1
uncertain_points.risk: Interrupted write may lead to an unterminated data word being ignored, causing HMAC length to be too short.

uncertain_points.claim: The accuracy of wmask_ones and its alignment with packer_ready is not verified here; if wmask_ones misrepresents the byte count, message_length_d becomes wrong.
uncertain_points.risk: HMAC length mismatch may occur, but likely caught by higher-level verification.
